problem: the reviewing agent F-04 identified memory inference outside the shared inference boundary. A mocked before-patch reproduction confirmed nonlocal destinations were accepted for embedding tags, embedding text and calibrated classification prompts.
change: Memory embedding and calibration now validate literal HTTP loopback destinations. A private urllib transport ignores environment proxies and installed global openers and refuses redirects. Validation occurs again at each request. Extraction is covered through calibration.classify. Existing unavailable-model fallback remains explicit.
validation: Five isolated unittest cases passed: 11 forbidden URL forms rejected before transport in both paths; real synthetic loopback responses for tags/embedding/extraction; hostile environment proxy received no requests; five redirect statuses reached no second server; embedding POST redirect and post-construction destination change refused; cascade fallback retained. Five calibrated-label assertions and 26 memory-privacy assertions passed. Before reproduction, raw logs, repeatable runner and stable hashes saved in experiments/product/memory-egress/.
limitations: No real model call or live service restart. Source fix is not proof the current running processes loaded it. Client transport containment only: a trusted local server can relay data. Not a system-wide leakage experiment or new egress telemetry integration. Nonliteral localhost names, LAN model servers and HTTPS endpoints are deliberately refused under the existing local-provider contract. Main SESSION_STATE untouched; coordination handoff provided.
